## What you're scoping
GitHub PR #65, ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa: "feat(header): global header rebuild — shell, logo, Contentful nav data, close-state contract (SFCC-52/746/747)". 104 files, +10187/-745, base develop.

- HEAD (10eb79dc881b3e3881d528ee661090779dc11b9d): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/bfb1292b-bdc6-483e-a9c4-1846dc9424fe/scratchpad/pr65-head
- BASE (269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/bfb1292b-bdc6-483e-a9c4-1846dc9424fe/scratchpad/pr65-base

Full PR description (for reference, verify claims against actual code, don't take it at face value):

---
Rebuilds the global header per SFCC-52 and its successor stories (SFCC-746 nav bar, SFCC-747 logo). Built as six independently-implemented branches, merged for integrated local testing, plus follow-on Contentful and i18n work done directly on this branch once testing surfaced real gaps.

Explicitly NOT in this PR: SFCC-93 (scroll behaviour, no design AC yet), header region selector and 3 logo behaviour scenarios (HPC-016, no Figma frame provided).

Known follow-ups (not blocking, flagged): list-menu.stories.tsx still tests the old root/categories prop shape (ListMenu now self-fetches, story renders incorrectly, needs rewrite); RightBar's Wishlist/Account icons call commerce hooks directly despite the component's own JSDoc claiming container/presentational separation; gallery/galleryItem/imageAndText Contentful types exist live in dev but are deliberately excluded from this PR's tracked template.
---

## The three tickets this PR claims (read them yourself in Jira for full text — I'm giving you the load-bearing parts)
- **SFCC-52** "Global Header UI": header shell/layout ONLY — visual structure, component placement, sticky behaviour. Icon destinations wired up in their own later stories (exception: logo links home). Labels include HPC-015/016/018/019/020/021/026/027 (functional-requirement-sheet cross-references — the actual requirement text lives in a spreadsheet I don't have live access to; if you can't verify one, say so rather than guessing).
- **SFCC-746** "Navigation – PWA Kit & Contentful": supersedes the nav portion of SFCC-52. Explicitly OUT of scope: "hover/focus/active visual states (defined in UI kit)". Explicitly states mega-menu behaviour AND mobile hamburger/drill-down are SFCC-96's scope, not 746's.
- **SFCC-747** "Logo Masthead": supersedes the logo portion of SFCC-52. Scroll behaviour out of scope (→ SFCC-93, still "To Do", no AC). Hover/focus states defined in UI kit, not repeated here.

## The scope question that actually matters most here
**SFCC-96** ("Expanded Navigation - PWA Kit and Contentful", status "Ready For Review", assignee Isabel Chaloner) describes: a desktop mega-menu opening on hover/click of a top-level nav item, two-column panel (subcategory + editorial links left, large campaign image right), all content Contentful-managed, close control top-right. **SFCC-97** ("Expanded Navigation Mobile") was archived 2026-08-24 with the note "Archiving as all breakpoints are covered in SFCC-96" — meaning SFCC-96 now also covers mobile hamburger drill-down (top-level categories, drill into subcategories, back control, Z.Immerse and "Back in Boutique" as direct links, CMS-managed items).

This PR ships `overrides/app/components/list-menu/megaMenuContent/` (desktop mega-menu, two-column, Contentful-driven, campaign image) and `overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/` (mobile drill-down with back navigation, Contentful-driven) in full, with extensive motion/animation and accessibility work behind both. Your job: read SFCC-96's actual described acceptance behaviour and compare it directly against what's actually implemented in `list-menu/megaMenuContent/` and `drawer-menu/` at HEAD. Give a factual verdict on how much of SFCC-96 this PR actually delivers — fully, partially, or negligibly — and cite specifics (which described behaviours exist in code, which don't). This PR's title and description never mention SFCC-96. That's not yours to fix or judge as right/wrong — just establish the factual overlap precisely so the human reviewer can decide what to do about it (e.g. whether this PR should also close/reference SFCC-96).

## A second, smaller scope question
The PR's tip commit (10eb79dc881b3e3881d528ee661090779dc11b9d itself, not a merge — "fix(footer): wrap site-map columns under subscribe until 946px") modifies `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` to change a footer breakpoint, with an inline comment reading "No confirmed Figma frame yet." Footer is not mentioned anywhere in SFCC-52/746/747's descriptions or this PR's own body/summary. Check `git log --oneline 269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99..10eb79dc881b3e3881d528ee661090779dc11b9d -- overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` — there's a second, earlier commit touching the same file (`fix(theme): centralize outer container padding into gridSystem.ts`) that IS legitimately in-scope (gridSystem.ts's container-padding token is explicitly shared by header/footer/main-content, so footer necessarily needs to consume it once header's own padding source changes) — don't confuse the two. Isolate just the 946px breakpoint change and judge whether it reads as legitimate incidental footer maintenance while working in adjacent territory, or as an out-of-scope addition riding along in a header PR with no ticket and no confirmed design source. Check whether any open Jira ticket already covers a footer sitemap/subscribe breakpoint at 946px before concluding there's no tracking for it.

## What to check for under-delivery too
Don't only look for scope creep — check whether SFCC-52/746/747's own stated ACs are actually all met. In particular: SFCC-52's header-shell responsive behaviour (desktop AND mobile, per its description), SFCC-746's Contentful-managed top-level nav items keyed by SFCC category ID, SFCC-747's logo accessibility/responsive-sizing/link-behaviour. Also sanity-check the PR's own "explicitly NOT in this PR" claims (SFCC-93 scroll, HPC-016 region selector + 3 logo scenarios) actually match what's in Jira/Figma rather than just trusting the PR's paraphrase — SFCC-93 is easy to check (still "To Do", no AC — confirmed by me already, matches). HPC-016 you'll need to judge from context since the underlying requirements spreadsheet isn't available to either of us; say plainly if you can't verify it rather than asserting it.

## Output
A scope verdict: does this PR deliver SFCC-52/746/747 (fully/partially, cite gaps if any), and a precise, evidence-based account of the SFCC-96 overlap and the footer-946px question. Cite file:line for every claim about what code does or doesn't do.

/**
 * Shared menu-expansion state contract for the header's LeftBar/RightBar sections.
 *
 * Confirmed via Figma review (SFCC-52 follow-up): desktop/tablet, mobile-L1 (root drawer)
 * and mobile-L2 (drilled into a category) each have a *different* close-state treatment —
 * there is no single uniform "close button" shared across breakpoints. Modelled as a flat,
 * behaviour-named discriminated union (per typescript.md's "discriminated unions for
 * variant/state modeling") rather than nested per-breakpoint booleans, since the four states
 * are mutually exclusive and each maps to exactly one rendering contract in LeftBar/RightBar.
 *
 * Naming is behaviour-first, not breakpoint-first: desktop and tablet share the identical
 * `fullSwap` treatment (see RightBar), so there is no separate `expandedDesktop`/
 * `expandedTablet` pair, and the two mobile drawer depths get their own state each because
 * their rendering contracts genuinely differ (`mobileL1` is a same-control icon toggle,
 * `mobileL2` adds a back control on the left and a close control on the right).
 *
 * **Scope note for SFCC-96/97 (real wiring):** this branch (infra only) does not manage or
 * derive this value from any real mega-menu/drawer open state — `LeftBar`/`RightBar` both
 * default their `menuExpanded` prop to `'closed'` and the header shell
 * (`header/index.tsx`) does not pass one at all. Wiring a real value in here — driven by
 * the actual mega-menu/drawer open/close/drill-in state — is that follow-up work's job.
 */
export type MenuExpandedState =
  | 'closed'
  // Desktop/tablet: a mega menu or drawer is open. RightBar's entire icon cluster (search,
  // profile, wishlist, bag) is replaced by a single "Close" text + X control.
  | 'fullSwap'
  // Mobile: the root drawer (L1) is open. LeftBar's hamburger toggles to an X in place —
  // nothing else changes; RightBar is unaffected (search + bag stay as in 'closed').
  | 'mobileL1'
  // Mobile: drilled into a category from the root drawer (L2). LeftBar shows a back
  // chevron (returns to L1, does not close the drawer). RightBar keeps search + bag
  // visible and adds a close X alongside them — no account/wishlist icons at this depth.
  | 'mobileL2';

## Scope Verdict — PR #65 (`feat(header): global header rebuild`)

### 1. Tier 1 hard stop — found, and it's unambiguous

Six files in this diff sit inside two distinct Tier 1 categories from `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`:

**Design System (`overrides/app/theme/foundation/`, Owner: UI Designer):**
- `overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts` — rewrites `containerPadding` from the documented `{base:'30px', md:'24px', xl:'0'}` to `{base: spacing['2xl'], md: spacing['2xl'], xl: spacing['3xl']}` and adds a new `maxWidth` token.
- `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts` — adds `--zimm-grid-max-width`.

**Test & Tooling Config (Owner: Integration/SI Partner):**
- `.storybook/main.js` — adds a webpack alias forcing `@tanstack/react-query` to a single physical file.
- `.storybook/preview.tsx` — adds a `window.__CONFIG__` shim and swaps the a11y exclude list to an import.
- `.storybook/a11yExcludes.ts` — new file under `.storybook/`.
- `vitest.config.ts` — adds an exact-match alias for `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`.

Every one of these is a real, substantive change (not a no-op or formatting diff — confirmed by reading each full diff above), and none of them is `.claude/registry/*.md` (which I've correctly excluded as expected auto-regen churn — `.claude/registry/components.md`, `hooks.md`, `pages.md`, `utils.md` are the only `.claude/**` paths touched, and that's the documented regeneration behavior, not a finding).

This alone is dispositive. Per this task's own rules, a Tier 1 touch is a hard stop regardless of how well the rest of the PR is scoped, and it also trips Hard Rule #10 (more than one protection tier touched — here it's two Tier-1 categories plus three Tier-2 categories: Global Shell, Contentful Schema Definitions, Translations).

I'm reporting the rest of what was asked below because it's genuinely useful for the human reviewer, but the verdict itself is fixed by the above.

### 2. SFCC-52 / SFCC-746 / SFCC-747 — mostly delivered, a few real gaps/questions

**Met, with evidence:**
- Responsive shell, desktop+mobile: `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:65-87` (`HEADER_CONTENT_SX`) and `:52-57` (`HEADER_LOGO_SX`) both key off explicit `base/sm/md/lg/xl/2xl` breakpoints; mobile drawer vs. desktop nav split is driven by `useHeaderMenuExpandedState` (`overrides/app/hooks/useHeaderMenuExpandedState.ts:42-95`).
- Logo links home: base `_app/index.jsx:278` defines `onLogoClick = () => navigate('/')` and passes it straight through; `header/index.tsx:258-268` wires it to the `<Button>` wrapping `<ZimmLogo>`.
- Logo accessibility/responsive sizing: `zimmLogo/index.tsx:42-43` (`aria-label`, `role="img"`), `header/index.tsx:56` (26px mobile → 74px tablet/desktop).
- Contentful-managed top-level nav items: `overrides/app/hooks/useHeaderNav.ts` + `scripts/contentful/content-types/headerNavItem.js`/`headerNavigation.js` — confirmed live content-type-driven, region-scoped.

**Real gap:** SFCC-746 is paraphrased as requiring nav items "keyed by SFCC category ID." `headerNavItem.js:21-49` has no `categoryId`/`category` field anywhere — only a free-text `href` Symbol field, explicitly documented as CMA-unenforceable ("exactly one of `href` or a non-empty `columns` should be set… CMA has no way to enforce this structurally"). Items are Contentful-managed, but keyed by manually-typed URL strings, not by a structured SFCC category reference. I can't confirm from the paraphrase alone whether literal category-ID keying was a hard AC or a looser description of intent — flagging factually rather than asserting a violation.

**Worth a judgment call, not a clean violation:** SFCC-746 excludes "hover/focus/active visual states (defined in UI kit)." This PR ships a dedicated underline-hover-animation system (`growUnderline` prop throughout `zimmNavItem`, commit `0b1e706` "nav underline animation," `useMegaMenuMotion.ts`). Whether that crosses the stated exclusion or is just the mechanical open/close behavior (distinct from "visual state styling") isn't resolvable without the UI kit doc — flagging for the reviewer.

**Confirmed correctly excluded:** SFCC-93 scroll behavior — no scroll-hide/shrink code anywhere in header (only unrelated `preventDefault`-the-page-scroll keyboard-handling comments in `list-menu-trigger.test.tsx:170` and `useHeaderNavKeyboard.test.ts:107`), matches the PR's claim and your own prior confirmation. HPC-016 (region selector) — no region/language-selector code found anywhere in header/list-menu/drawer-menu; I cannot verify this against the requirements spreadsheet itself, so I'm not asserting full compliance, only that nothing in the diff contradicts the claim.

### 3. SFCC-96 overlap — substantial, not partial

Comparing SFCC-96's described behavior directly against code at HEAD:

| SFCC-96 description | Delivered? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Opens on hover/click of L1 item | Yes | `list-menu-trigger.tsx:70` (`onMouseOver={onOpen}`) + Chakra's injected click/Enter/Space activation, plus explicit Space handling at `:79-82` |
| Two-column panel | Yes | `toMegaMenuItem.ts:44-49` (`twoColumnLayout` splits into 2 columns via `splitEvenly`) |
| Subcategory + editorial links, left | Yes | `megaMenuContent/index.tsx:98-116` (`SectionColumn` renders CMS-driven `MegaMenuSection.links`, content-agnostic) |
| Large campaign image, right | Yes | `megaMenuContent/index.tsx:150-154` (`promoImage` rendered via `<Image>`), backed by dedicated commits `3ebf181`/`268c0a8` for responsive/smart-cropped Contentful images |
| All content Contentful-managed | Yes | `headerNavItem.js`, `navGroup.js`, `link.js`, `image.js` content types; `useHeaderNav.ts` fetch |
| Close control, top-right | Yes (functionally) | `rightBar/index.tsx:175-185` — `fullSwap` state replaces the entire right-side icon cluster with a "Close" + X control, wired through `useMegaMenuOpenReporter`/`header/index.tsx:156-176`. It's the header's shared right-side control, not an icon embedded inside the panel's own corner — a reasonable but not literal match to "top-right of the panel." |

For the SFCC-97-absorbed mobile scope (drill-down, back control, direct links):
- L1 categories, L1→L2 drill: `drawer-menu/index.tsx:54-79, 86-119`.
- Back control: **exists**, but lives on the header shell's `LeftBar` (back-chevron), not inside `DrawerMenu` itself — `leftBar/index.tsx:57-61` (`case 'mobileL2': ... menuOnClick = onBack`), wired via `useHeaderMenuExpandedState.ts:64-67` (`handleBack`).
- Direct-link items (Z.Immerse-style): the component generically supports href-only, no-column items and this exact shape is exercised in tests/stories (`drawer-menu/index.test.tsx:149-151`, `list-menu.test.tsx:97-117`) using "Z.Immerse" as the fixture label. "Back in Boutique" itself doesn't appear anywhere in code — expected, since this is CMS-authored content, not something the component hardcodes.
- CMS-managed: same `useHeaderNav()` fetch as desktop.

One real, self-disclosed gap: `drawer-menu/index.tsx:85` states plainly "No Figma motion spec exists for the L1<->L2 transition, so this swap is instant — a deliberate placeholder." So mobile drill-down has no real transition, unlike desktop's extensive motion work.

**Notable:** two in-repo comments are now stale and understate what's actually wired — `headerTypes.ts:12-20`'s "Scope note for SFCC-96/97… this branch (infra only) does not manage or derive this value from any real mega-menu/drawer open state" and `leftBar/index.tsx:19` ("Not wired to any real mega-menu/drawer state on this branch") are both contradicted by `header/index.tsx:156-203`, which does wire real `isMegaMenuOpen`/`mobileMenuExpanded` state. This is evidence the PR delivers *more* of SFCC-96/97 than its own internal doc trail admits — reinforcing that this is a real, close-to-complete implementation, not a stub.

**Bottom line on SFCC-96:** this PR delivers the substantial majority of SFCC-96's (and the SFCC-97-absorbed mobile) described acceptance behavior in code. Neither this PR's title, body, nor summary mention SFCC-96 anywhere.

### 4. Footer — two separate over-delivery findings, not one

**a) The tip commit's 946px change (`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, commit `10eb79d`):** isolated from the legitimate `9a1d3d9` gridSystem-centralization commit (which I confirm is properly in-scope — it consumes the exact same `var(--zimm-grid-margin-*)` tokens `header/index.tsx:71-86` consumes, a genuine shared-token dependency). The 946px change is different in kind: it introduces a brand-new `BP_CONTENT_WRAP` constant unrelated to the shared grid tokens, purely a footer layout-wrap redesign. Its own inline comment says "No confirmed Figma frame yet" and the commit message cites "per design feedback" (not a ticket). I have no Jira/Atlassian tool in this session to positively confirm or rule out a tracking ticket — flagging that limitation rather than asserting there is none. What I can confirm: no ticket number appears in the commit message or PR body, and no `.docs/` file mentions 946px or this footer wrap behavior.

**b) A second, separate footer thread I found independently while building the manifest:** `scripts/contentful/content-types/footerConfig.js` gains three new fields (`phoneLabel`/`whatsAppLabel`/`emailLabel`), wired through `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:83-88,116-121`, `footerNavColumn/index.tsx:21-27,102-109`, and `zimmContactIconRow/index.tsx:15-20,55-62` — making footer contact-link labels CMS-editable where they were previously hardcoded constants. This is new footer capability with no connection to header/nav/logo, arriving via the `feature/contentful-cleanup` branch merge (`6d8ec03`). It's distinct from the legitimate `FooterNavGroupEntry→NavGroupEntry` rename also present in these same files, which *is* properly in-scope (directly caused by header's mega-menu needing to reuse the same `navGroup` shape — `scripts/contentful/content-types/navGroup.js:6-10` says so explicitly).

### 5. A third over-delivery item, found independently: `overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx`

New copy-first override of base SFCC's `HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile`, moving the mobile/desktop split from `lg` (992px) to `md` (768px). This is a shared, app-wide utility. I checked its actual consumers: `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx` (pre-existing PDP file, unrelated to header) is a real, active consumer whose rendering behavior changes app-wide as a result. Inside this PR's own header code, the only reference to `HideOnDesktop` is dead/commented-out (`header/index.tsx:273`). So this change has zero live effect on anything this PR ships, but a confirmed live effect on PDP — a different page, arguably a different squad's territory — with no mention in the PR body.

### 6. One boundary case worth flagging, not a violation

`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSearchInput/index.tsx` is a fully working search box — types, submits on Enter, writes session recent-search history, and navigates via `searchUrlBuilder` (`:54-60`). The PR body says "icon destinations wired up in their own later stories (exception: logo links home)" — naming exactly one exception. Search doesn't cleanly fit "icon" or "logo," and it's a real, working destination, not a shell stub — worth the reviewer's judgment on whether this was meant to ship now.

### Verdict

**BLOCKED** — `overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts` and `overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts` (Design System, Tier 1, UI-Designer-owned) and `.storybook/main.js`, `.storybook/preview.tsx`, `.storybook/a11yExcludes.ts` (new), and `vitest.config.ts` (Test & Tooling Config, Tier 1, Integration/SI-Partner-owned) are all substantively modified in this diff. Per Hard Rule #2/#4/#8 and `frozenFiles.md`, none of these may be merged without a named owner's approval — this is a hard stop, not a judgment call, independent of everything else in this PR.

Separately from the blocking issue, for the human reviewer's disposition once Tier 1 approval is sought: this PR also carries real, evidenced over-delivery (the footer 946px breakpoint with no confirmed Figma frame and no located ticket; the unrelated footerConfig contact-label content-model addition; `responsive/index.tsx`'s app-wide, PDP-affecting breakpoint change with no live header consumer) and a substantial undisclosed overlap with SFCC-96 (and the SFCC-97-absorbed mobile scope) that neither the PR title nor body references anywhere.
